title: M5Unified PR #447 PCF8563 keep timer running across begin()

hardware.reason: No CoreInk or other PCF8563 board available locally or in the hardware test center; only the M5Dial virtual profile provides a PCF8563 model.
hardware.devices_considered: matrix, corep4, sticks3, stopwatch (hardware test center); none is a PCF8563 board

execution.environment: macOS arm64; local ESP-IDF v6.0.2; Device Service dial profile (M5Dial, QEMU, PCF8563 register model)

checks.detail: Both variants built from pinned local checkouts with IDF_COMPONENT_MANAGER=0; merged BIN 503936 bytes each.
M5Dial QEMU session booted the sketch and returned PCF8563 register readbacks over I2C (TC/C2/CNT).
PR keeps 0x82 across M5.begin() and a second Rtc.begin(); a stopped 0x00 is normalised to 0x03; 0x83 is preserved; disableIRQ() leaves 0x03. Base rewrites to 0x03/0x00 as expected.
Timer countdown and TF/INT firing after begin() cannot be observed: the QEMU PCF8563 model has no countdown logic. Author's CoreInk hardware result remains the only evidence for that.

notes: PR description is English; the published comment is English.
Comment posted once; PR remains OPEN; no approval, merge, close or push.
The PR patch applies cleanly to base 11bfd4b (git apply --check).
Non-blocking review note: begin() now fails if the new 0x0E read fails, where it previously needed only writes; the driver already depends on reads for the RTC time registers.
